text:
Cutter Gauthier's goal on Sunday was the least likely of the night, a 2% chance by our model, and it hardly mattered how it went in. That's nine straight games with a goal for the Ducks winger, and it put Anaheim 2-0 up on Calgary midway through the first on its way to a 6-1 win at Honda Center.

The Ducks didn't need luck beyond that. They took 70 shot attempts to Calgary's 55 and created 5.23 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.74, which is about as one-sided as the league gets. Jeff Malott, an undrafted free agent who worked up from the ECHL, opened the scoring 1:16 in. Tyson Hinds, a third-round pick out of Rimouski, assisted on Gauthier's goal for his first NHL point and added another assist later.

The second was scoreless, mostly because Devin Cooley kept it that way, but the third was a flood. Tim Washe scored early on a 36% chance, and after Mikael Backlund got Calgary on the board at 4:04, Beckett Sennecke answered 25 seconds later with a slapshot. Sennecke added a backhand at 16:14 for his second, and Mikael Granlund finished it under a minute later. Sennecke finished with two goals and an assist and 1.42 expected goals of his own, the busiest player on the ice.

Ville Husso, first star, made 20 saves on 21 shots and stopped 1.7 more goals than expected. He was the biggest contributor to Anaheim's win by our numbers, which says something about how few dangerous looks Calgary produced; the Flames also gave the puck away 21 times. Cooley allowed five on 33 shots, a little worse than expected but hardly the problem.

This was the fourth meeting already, and Anaheim has won three of them. For Calgary, coming off a win in Los Angeles, it's a reminder that the blue line has been thinner since Kevin Bahl's season-ending injury. For the Ducks, it's another night where the kids and the veterans scored together, and another day for Gauthier to keep the streak headlines coming.
headline: Gauthier makes it nine straight as Ducks rout Flames
